title: Flat lower truncation and its bounded-above K-flat kernel
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $T$ a scheme. Work on a small skeleton of $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site; def-weil-size-convention] with constant ring sheaf $\Lambda_T$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Let $K^\bullet$ be an integer-indexed cochain complex of $\Lambda_T$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and let $a\in\mathbf Z$. Assume $H^i(K^\bullet)=0$ for every $i<a$ [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] and assume that $N=\operatorname{coker}(d^{a-1}:K^{a-1}\to K^a)$ is flat. Put $P^\bullet=\tau_{\ge a}K^\bullet$ [def-kun-truncations], with terms $0$ for $i<a$, $N$ for $i=a$, and $K^i$ for $i>a$, and differential out of $N$ induced by $d^a$. Let $q:K^\bullet\to P^\bullet$ be zero below $a$, the cokernel projection at $a$, and the identity above $a$. Then $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] and $P^\bullet$ has flat terms. Its kernel $L^\bullet$ has terms $K^i$ for $i<a$, $I=\operatorname{im}(d^{a-1})$ for $i=a$, and $0$ for $i>a$, with the differential $K^{a-1}\to I$ the image factorization of $d^{a-1}$. The sheaf $I$ is flat, $L^\bullet$ is bounded above with flat terms and is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], and $0\to L^\bullet\to K^\bullet\xrightarrow{q}P^\bullet\to0$ is short exact in every degree.

source.place: Tag 0F1M (lemma-bounded-below-tor-amplitude), lower truncation and kernel paragraphs

proof.text: Write $p:K^a\twoheadrightarrow N$ for the cokernel projection and $I=\operatorname{im}d^{a-1}$. Since $d^ad^{a-1}=0$, the cokernel universal property gives a unique $\bar d:N\to K^{a+1}$ with $\bar d p=d^a$. Moreover $d^{a+1}\bar d=0$, since its composite with the epimorphism $p$ is zero. Together with the retained differentials this defines $P=\tau_{\ge a}K$ as in [def-kun-truncations]. The components $q^i=0$ for $i<a$, $q^a=p$, and $q^i=1$ for $i>a$ obey the chain-map equations of [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]: at $a-1$ this is $pd^{a-1}=0$, at $a$ it is $\bar d p=d^a$, and elsewhere it is immediate.

source.place: Tag 0F1M (lemma-bounded-below-tor-amplitude), proof: lower truncation and its kernel

proof.text: Compute the maps on cohomology using [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules]. For $i<a$, both cohomology sheaves are zero by the hypothesis and the zero terms of $P$. At $a$, because $I\subseteq\ker d^a$, the kernel of $\bar d:K^a/I\to K^{a+1}$ is $(\ker d^a)/I$; this is $H^a(K)$ and $H^a(q)$ is the resulting identification. At $a+1$, the cycles are unchanged and the boundaries are unchanged because $\operatorname{im}\bar d=\operatorname{im}d^a$ (the map $p$ is epic). In all higher degrees the adjacent terms and differentials are unchanged. Thus $H^i(q)$ is an isomorphism in every degree, which is precisely the quasi-isomorphism assertion of [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules].

source.place: Tag 0F1M (lemma-bounded-below-tor-amplitude), proof: lower truncation and its kernel

proof.text: The kernels of the components of $q$ are $K^i$ for $i<a$, $I=\ker p$ for $i=a$, and zero for $i>a$. The induced differential from degree $a-1$ to $a$ is the image factorization $K^{a-1}\twoheadrightarrow I$ of $d^{a-1}$; all earlier differentials are retained and the differential out of $I$ is zero. These differentials square to zero, by the equations for $K$ and the monomorphism $I\hookrightarrow K^a$, so they define the kernel complex $L$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Every $q^i$ is epic, and the degreewise sequences are $0\to K^i\xrightarrow{1}K^i\to0\to0$ for $i<a$, $0\to I\to K^a\xrightarrow{p}N\to0$ for $i=a$, and $0\to0\to K^i\xrightarrow{1}K^i\to0$ for $i>a$. This proves the claimed degreewise short exact sequence.

source.place: Tag 0F1M (lemma-bounded-below-tor-amplitude), proof: lower truncation and its kernel

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-quotient-tensor-ses] to $0\to I\to K^a\to N\to0$ on the chosen small site with ring sheaf $\Lambda_T$. Its middle term $K^a$ is flat by the termwise-flat hypothesis and its quotient $N$ is flat by assumption, so its kernel-flatness clause gives that $I$ is flat. The zero sheaf is flat because tensoring with it is the zero exact functor [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Consequently every term of $P$ is flat: its terms are zero, $N$, or retained terms of $K$. Likewise every term of $L$ is flat: its terms are retained terms of $K$, $I$, or zero.

source.place: Tag 03EY (lemma-flat-ses), part (2), sheaf case; applied in Tag 0F1M

proof.text: The explicit terms give $L^i=0$ for all $i>a$, so $a$ is an upper bound for $L$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-kun-kflat-criteria] to this bounded-above complex of flat $\Lambda_T$-module sheaves. It gives that $L$ is K-flat in the convention of [def-kun-derived-tensor] used by that node; by the sign symmetry recorded in [def-kun-derived-tensor] this is the ringed-site K-flatness of [def-pc-kflat-complex] asserted in the statement. This completes all the assertions.

It is not in the dropped list, cites no SGA, adds no new nodes, and no other group has split it. It matches the Stacks proof of 0F1M: E=tau_{>=a}K, kernel L=(...->K^{a-1}->I->0), I flat from 0->I->K^a->N->0, and L bounded above with flat terms is K-flat (06YQ). The direction K->P is correct; the parent's main-20261015 text writes the arrow the other way in one sentence. Step 1: the cokernel universal property gives the induced differential, and the chain-map equations check out against def-kun-truncations. Step 2: H^a(P)=ker d^a/I, im of the induced differential = im d^a because p is epi, and the vanishing for i<a (including a-1) is used. Step 3: the kernel complex and the three degreewise exact sequences are elementary and correct. Step 4: lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-quotient-tensor-ses applies (small skeleton, Lambda_T commutative, N and K^a flat). This off-unit generic tool is declared in split_report.tool_uses and I accept it; the Kunneth unit has no such node, and no duplicate exists (lem-sc-affine-truncation-kernel-flat and lem-pc-derived-lower-truncation-step-ses are different statements). Step 5: lem-kun-kflat-criteria(1) holds under the same hypotheses. Small cases checked: the contractible [F->F] gives P=0 and L=K; a nonzero term in degree a-1 or Z--2-->Z would break the conclusion, and the hypotheses exclude both.
